text:
Ana: Heads-up — cloud marketplace strategy sync. AWS asked about a private-offer template for Dedicated + Private bundles. Thinking: 12m committed spend, 15–20% off list, incremental discount for 24m. Thoughts?
Sophie: 15–20% sounds reasonable for mid-market. For enterprise deals sales will still want room to negotiate. Can we add an extra SI incentive line for partners that bring pipeline? :thinking_face:
Mike: Quick math: 15% on hosted ARR reduces rev by ~11% post-marketplace fees. For Dedicated (reserved capacity) margins are higher but we need guardrails. Proposal: tiered discounts: 12m -> 12%, 24m -> 18%, 36m -> 22% with minimum committed $100k.
Clara: Need to preserve gross margin floor. If marketplace takes 5–7% and we give 22% on 36m, our net could be thin for some SKUs. Suggest cap discount by SKU family (e.g., quantized models vs large LLMs). Also require prepayment or annual invoicing for the deeper discounts.
Raj: From legal: avoid language that auto-renews discounts without explicit renewal conversation. Private offers should have explicit renewal term + a 60–90 day notice window for pricing changes. Also add a clause restricting resale/transfer if we include SI credits.
Tom: Ops note: Dedicated SKU must be named consistently across marketplace and our pricing engine so quotas/rollouts map. If discount is applied to a bundle, ensure billing tags contain model_version + deployment_type. Otherwise routing/fallback gets messy.
Ana: Good call. Let's keep the marketplace private-offer payload simple but with clear metadata. Draft of offer structure I mocked:
```
offer_name: "Redwood Dedicated - 24m Commit"
commit_term_months: 24
commit_minimum_usd: 250000
discount_matrix: [ {tier: "base", discount_pct: 18}, {tier: "si_referral", discount_pct: 22} ]
billing: "annual-invoice"
renewal_notice_days: 75
```
Sophie: Love the si_referral bump. Sales will want a promotional credit rather than outright discount in some cases — easier to preserve margin. Maybe allow either "discount_pct" or "si_credit_usd" in template.
Mike: We also need renewal pricing guardrails: for renewals keep discount <= prior discount + 2% unless finance signs off. Prevent perpetual discount escalation.
Clara: Agreed. Also require an internal approval workflow for any >18% discount on Dedicated or >15% on Hosted. Keep a log of approved private offers for audit.
Raj: Add a standard data-protection clause for private deployments (VPC/on-prem) in offers — partners sometimes push their own terms. Keep our DPA + KMS requirements as non-negotiable.
marketplace-bot: Created doc: /wiki/marketplace/private-offer-template (draft) — PR #432 opened by Ana
Tom: For engineering, flag: if partner requests multi-region capacity as part of commit, we need a dev ticket to reserve capacity pools. That changes cost assumptions.
Ana: Action items: (1) Mike to put together tiered P&L scenarios for 12/24/36m by SKU (due EOD Thu). (2) Clara + Raj to write approval + legal clauses for template (due Mon). (3) Sophie to run a quick win list of deals that could convert to private offers this quarter and note SI partners (due Wed). (4) Tom to add SKU naming + billing tag spec to PR (linked above).
Sophie: One more ask — can we coordinate joint announcement cadence with marketing? If we offer SI incentives, partners will want co-marketing. Recommend 4–6 week lead time from signed PO to announcement.
Ana: Yep — include marketing lead in the PR. We'll default to 6 weeks for joint announce unless partner asks for embargo.
Clara: Final: require minimum renewal notification to customers 90 days before expiry for any committed spend over $250k.
Ana: Thanks all — will iterate on the draft PR. We'll reconvene after Mike's P&L. :thumbsup:
